title: Adaptive microburst cushioning for mixed-priority inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an adaptive headroom and smoothing layer ("microburst cushion") that budgets GPU memory across weights, KV cache, and activations to absorb short-duration inference spikes from mixed-priority traffic while minimizing cold KV eviction and throughput loss.
background: We observe transient bursts from low-latency customers and batch backfills that cause immediate KV eviction or activation OOMs. Current safety policies use static soft watermarks and binary preemption which either waste headroom or cause frequent quality-impacting KV evictions. The goal is a runtime-side control plane that allocates a small, dynamic cushion per-GPU that grows/shrinks with measured request arrival patterns, continuous-batching state, and recent eviction history.
proposed_solution: Introduce a per-GPU microburst-reserve counter (MR-counter) representing ephemeral headroom in bytes, distinct from long-term reservations for weights.
Feed MR-counter adjustments with three signals: short-window arrival rate, live KV hit/eviction rate, and active continuous-batching depth.
Smooth eviction signals using an EWMA with configurable half-life to avoid toggling during noisy spikes.

When MR-counter is positive, allow activations to allocate up to the cushion without triggering KV eviction; if exhausted, trigger graded degradation (batch size reduction -> slow-path fallbacks -> eviction) rather than immediate wholesale eviction.
Integrate MR-counter with existing reserve ledger so dedicated capacity customers can opt-in with different cushion multipliers.
Expose control knobs in console: target cushion ratio, smoothing window, graded-degradation policy, and min-kv-retention threshold.
Add a lightweight simulation harness to test mixed-priority traces against the policy before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated with cushion concepts and operational thresholds.
No increase in 95th percentile latency for high-priority traffic after enabling cushion under synthetic mixed-loads.
KV eviction rate reduces by >= 40% during 10–60s microbursts in our offline workload replay tests compared to baseline.
Memory accounting telemetry shows MR-counter toggling appropriately and fallback steps being exercised on at least one cluster during canary rollout.
Feature gate and per-customer multiplier exist; default off for existing Dedicated customers until opt-in.
experiments: Offline replay of mixed workloads (LLM-chat bursty traffic + nightly batch) on 8-GPU node: baseline eviction spikes at 37 evictions/min, with MR-cushion reduced to 13 evictions/min (approx -65%).
Microbenchmark: enabling EWMA smoothing with 3s half-life prevents two-thirds of toggles observed with raw signal on 30s noisy trace.
Latency impact: end-to-end 95p for high-priority queries change within ±1% under controlled replay.
Memory headroom overhead measured at steady-state ~4.5% of total GPU RAM with default cushion ratio 0.05.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-tuned cushion leads to underutilized GPU memory and increased unit cost. Mitigation: conservative default (0.03), per-customer multipliers, and autoscaling knob to reduce cushion when utilization drops.
Risk: Complexity interacts poorly with existing KV prefetch/eviction. Mitigation: implement graded-degradation with instrumentation points and feature flag to revert behavior quickly.
Risk: Bursts longer than cushion duration still cause eviction. Mitigation: detect sustained burst (>window) and transition to fallback model routing policy (route to compatible variant or throttle).
telemetry_and_alerting: KV eviction rate, KV hit rate, and activation allocation failures annotated with MR-counter state.
Metric: fraction of allocations that consumed MR vs normal pool.
Alert: sustained MR exhaustion > 30s with rising eviction rate -> Pager (SEV2).
Dashboard tile in Console: cushion usage heatmap and playback of recent microbursts.
test_plan: Unit tests for MR-counter arithmetic and smoothing logic.
Integration test: simulate continuous-batching and mixed-priority traffic inside CI harness with deterministic seeds.
Load tests: replay production traces in a staging cluster with and without cushion to validate eviction and latency targets.
Chaos test: induce GPU memory pressure and ensure graded-degradation path occurs and recovers cleanly.
notes: Related: look at continuous-batching backpressure primitives and KV retention heuristics before implementation.
Customer asks: two enterprise customers reported repeated quality regressions due to tail evictions during daytime bursts; discussed trade-offs with Solutions SE on 2026-03-09.
